first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both currently declining, and prior evidence links signup and onboarding simplification to durable activation and faster time-to-value. I would verify those results and also check the archived pricing evidence because competitor pressure creates a credible alternative. Run a guarded simplification test with qualified activation, downstream usage, retention, and revenue-quality guardrails so a completion lift does not mask weaker customer value.

final.rationale: Run a standard, segment-scoped onboarding simplification experiment focused on self-serve SMB accounts. Prior shortening improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, directly addressing both current declines; signup simplification also lifted SMB activation and qualified revenue, though its small retention decline requires guardrails. Measure activation, time-to-value, qualified revenue, and 30-day retention, with no rollout if retention or revenue quality deteriorates. Do not use promotional pricing because its acquisition lift was offset by a 12% renewal-cycle retention decline.
